# JesusCrust

## What This Is

A Rust/WASM-powered state and scheduling core for JavaScript UIs aimed at reducing lag in large, highly dynamic pages. It keeps DOM writes in JS while moving state graphs, diffing, and scheduling into Rust to cut allocation churn and batch updates.

## Core Value

Make complex, fast-updating web UIs feel responsive by minimizing main-thread work.

## Requirements

### Validated

(None yet — ship to validate)

### Active

- [ ] Rust/WASM reactive store with selectors and dependency tracking
- [ ] Patch-op pipeline plus JS host apply pass (batched per frame)
- [ ] Scheduling and batching (priority/time-slice aware)
- [ ] Built-in list virtualization primitive

### Out of Scope

- Full replacement UI runtime (React-class component model) in v1 — too large
- Devtools/IDE integrations — defer until core proves value
- Native desktop/mobile targets — web-only for now

## Context

Working name "JavaCrust" in early notes. The problem focus is main-thread jank from heavy DOM updates, GC churn, and over-rendering in large apps (feeds, chat, editors). The MVP should prove that Rust/WASM can own state + diff + scheduling while JS focuses on DOM patch application.

## Constraints

- **Platform**: Web + WASM only — keep APIs browser-compatible
- **Performance**: Reduce input latency under high-frequency updates
- **Boundary**: Cross JS↔WASM in batches to avoid per-node overhead
